open_obligations: Check whether the question-distribution part of the limitation is addressed.
Check that RL beating BC holds on full-book evaluation, not only on subtasks.
Check whether Wu et al.'s RL policies maximize a learned reward function, and if so whether it is learned from human comparisons at each node or from whole-book judgements.
out.other_title: Question distribution must cover all subquestions; supervised rather than reward learning
out.rationale: Christiano et al. note that in their experiments X is trained by supervised learning from Amplify_H(X), whereas in many important applications they suspect they would learn a reward function from Amplify_H(X) and train X to maximize it. Wu et al. report that their 175B RL policies significantly outperform their 175B BC baseline, though the improvement is smaller for the 6B models.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether recursive decomposition can be trained with learned rewards and RL rather than supervised learning, for book summarisation

text: The paper reports that training on only the first subtree does comparably to training on the full tree and generalises well to full-book summarisation, while the final 175B full-tree model was noticeably worse than the previous one. 175B RL policies significantly outperform the 175B behavioural-cloning baseline, with a smaller improvement at 6B.
title: RL beats behavioral cloning at 175B; first-subtree training generalizes to full tree
